segments.he: ארבעה אבו תנזייקן השור וכו'. ע"פ מ"ש במאמר וביום הביכורים (סי' נו) שמלכות הרשעה שהיא כנגד מלכות דקדושה מתגברת לאסוף ולכנוסממון כי שם כל הניצוצות הקדושה וע"כ היא מתגברת בתאוות ממון וכו'. אבל יש כח במלכות דקדושה להוציא בלעו מפיו בבחי' עת אשר שלט האדם באדם לרע לו שמוציאין מהם כל הקדושה ונעשה מזה תורה גבוה מאד דייקא וכו' ע"ש. ומלכות הרשעה הוא מלכות המן עמלק שרודף אחר מחנה דן בחי' מלכות דקודשה ע"ש:

וזה בחי' אבות נזיקין שהם בח'י מלכו תהרשעה שהם מזיקין ממון ישראל כי הם מתגברין על הממון לפגום אותו מחמת ששם כל הטוב כנ"ל. וע"כ הם ד' כי מלכות דקדושה היא בחי' ד' וכשנופל ונפגם בחי' הד' שהיא מלכות דקדושה אזי נעשה מזה בחי' ד' מלכיות שהם מלכות הרשעה בחי' עמלק שכלול מכל הד' מכליות כמובא כ"ז במאמר מישרא דסכינא (סי' ל') ע"כ הם מתגברי ןעל הממון להזיקו כי מלכות דקדושה תיקונה ושלימותה ע"י שונא בצע לשנוא הממון בתכלית השנאה כמבוא שם במאמר מישרא הנ"ל. וע"כ להיפך מלכות דס,א שהם הד' מלכיות מתגברין להזיק ממון ישראל דהיינו שמתגברין בתאוות ממון שבזה הם מזיקין ממון ישראל שפע קודש להכניסו אל התאוה שהיא מס"א ח"ו כי עיקר הגליות הם רק ע"י הממון כי שם כל הנצוצות הקודושת והם מתגברים להוציאם לחוץ ח"ו ע"י תאוות ממון וע"י מה שגוזלין לממון ישראל כי הם בחי' אחת דהיינו גזילתם ממש והתגברות התאוה על ישראל כי הכל כדי לינק ולקבל משפע קודש הגנוז בממון כנ"ל. אבל יש כח במלכות דקדושה להוציא בלעם מפיהם כנ"ל וזהבחי' שצריכים לשלם במיטב כ"ש מיטב שדהו וכו'. כי מוציאין כל הטוב מהם ואדרבא אפי' כל הניצוצות והטוב שהי' ביניהם מכבר מוציאין מהם ע"י שנתקבץ הטוב יחד ע"י שהתגברו וינקו עוד הרבה טוב שעי"ז נתקבץ ונתחבר ונדבק הניצוצות שהיו שם מכבר שלא הו יכולים לצאת ועכשיו נתחברים בזה הטוב הנ"ל. ואח"כ יוצא מהם הכל כנ"ל שזה בחי' עת אשר שלט האדם באדם לרע לו כי ע"י שליטתם והתגברותם נשאר אצלם הרע לבד בלי שום טוב שזהו מפלתם כי כל הטוב יוצא מהם. וזה בחי' מיטב שדהו ומיטב כרמו ישלם שכל הטוב שהי' כבוש ביניהם צריכים לשלם ולהחזיר לבעלים אל הקדושה כנ"ל:

וזה בחי' משארז"ל שהניזק והמזיק בתשלומין כי המת יהי' לו שהבעלים מטפלין בנבילה כי הניזקין שהם ישראל, שמתגברין עליהם המזיקין שהם האומות בתאוות ממון כנ"ל ועי"ז ניזק ממונם כנ"ל, הם צריכן לקבל את הנבילה המתה לטפל בה למכרה לברר הטוב והחיות דהיינו ניצוצות הקדושה של ממון ישראל שנשאר בה עדיין. וזה מוטל על הבעלים הניזקין שהם הישראל כי להם לבד זההכח לברר ולהוציא הטוב מן המתים והנשברים כי גם הם חייבים בזה וראוי להם לסבול ג,כ קצת בהיזק כשרז"ל והניזק והמזיק בתשלומין שגם על הניזק חל תשלומי ההיזק. היינו שבודאי צריכין לתקן את אשר נמשכו אחריהם עד שניזוקו כי אנו צריכין לשמור אצמינו מ ןההיזק היינו לבלי למשוך אחר תאוותיהם כנ"ל, וע"כ כשלא שמרו עצמן עד שניזוקו מהם דהיינו שהתגברו עליהם כנ"ל צריכין לטפל בנבילה המתה לברר הטוב ממנה דהיינו הממון שנשאר בה כנ"ל. ומותר ההיזק מוציאין מן המזיקין שמעמידין אותן בדין וצריכין לשלם במיטב כנ"ל דהיינו שהתגברו עליהם כנ"ל צריכין לטפל בנבילה המתה לברר הטוב ממנה דהיינו הממון שנשאר בה כנ"ל. ומותר ההיזק מוציאין מן המזיקין שמעמידין אותן בדין וצריכין לשלם במיטב כנ"ל דהיינו שמוציאין הטוב מהם כנ"ל. וזה נעשה ע"י הג' דיינים כשרז"ל דיני נזיקין בשלשה כי הג' דיינים הם בח'י הג' אבות שהם בחי' שלש רגלים שבהם עולה המלכות ביניהם ואזי נכנע הס"א שהיא מלכות הרשעה היינו שמוציאין הטוב מהם שמשלמין במיטב כנ"ל וכש"ש לעיל בה' דיינים שזהבח'י ג' דיינים ע"ש:

וע"כ נקראי םאבות נזיקין כנגד מלכות דקדושה שעיקר שלימותה ע, יג' אבות כמובא שזה בחי' שלש רגלים כנ"ל כמובא במאמר מישרא הנ"ל, ואת זה לעומת זה מלכות הרשעה מקבלין מאבות הטומאה שעיקרם המת שהוא אבי אבות הטומאה שהוא בחי' עמלק כמובא, והם מקבלין משם כי הוא כלל כולם כ"ש ראשית גוים עמלק כ"ש רבינו ז"ל שם וע"כ נקרא מלכות הרשעה ד' אבות נזיקין:

וזה שאמרו במשנה לא הרי זה כהרי זה ולא הרי זה כהרי זה כי הם בחי' עולם הפירוד בחי' ומשם יפרד והיה לארבעה ראשים היפך מלכות דקדושה שהיא בחי' ד' דאחד בחי' אחדות פשוט. וע,כאין בהם אחדות והשתוות רק מופרדין ומוחלקין זה מזה ואין בהם צד השוה כ"א שדרכן להזיק כנ"ל וכשהזיק משלמין במיטב כנ"ל:
segments.he_nikud: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּשְׁנָה, לֹא הֲרֵי זֶה כַּהֲרֵי זֶה וְלֹא הֲרֵי זֶה כַּהֲרֵי זֶה, כִּי הֵם בְּחִינַת עוֹלַם הַפֵּרוּד, בְּחִינַת וּמִשָּׁם יִפָּרֵד וְהָיָה לְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁים הֵפֶךְ מַלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת ד' דְּאֶחָד בְּחִינַת אַחְדוּת פָּשׁוּט. וְעַל כֵּן אֵין בָּהֶם אַחְדוּת וְהִשְׁתַּוּוּת רַק מֻפְרָדִין וּמֻחְלָקִין זֶה מִזֶּה וְאֵין בָּהֶם צַד הַשָּׁוֶה כִּי אִם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לְהַזִּיק כַּנַּ"ל וּכְשֶׁהִזִּיק מְשַׁלְּמִין בְּמֵיטַב כַּנַּ"ל:

segments.he: ויש לפרש השור הואבחי' יון שאמרו כתבו לכם על קרן השור וכו' קרן השור דייקא בחי' השור שהואבחי' הקרן. והבור ה מלכות הרשעה מלכו תאדום שהוא עמלק שהוא מוכן לתקלה כי בור דא טחול לילילת אמא דע"ר תאות ניאוף שזה בחי' עמלק כמובא. והמבעה זה השן בחי' אכילה בחי' פרס ומיד שאוכלין בשר כדוב וכו' גם מדי התגברו על ישראל ע"י אכילה בימי אחשורוש על שנהנו מסעודתו של אותו רשע. וההבער זה בבל נבוכדנאצר שהבעיר אש בביהמ"ק. ואי ןמוכן לתקלה כמו הבור שהוא עמלק תאוה הלכליות רע הכולל כיכלול מכולם כנ"ל. וזה שארז"ל אי כתב בור וחד מינייהו הוי ילפינין כולהו כי בור כלול מכולם שהוא בחי'מלכות עמלק שכלול מכולם כנ, לוממנו נלמדין כולם כי הכל נלמדו ממנו, כשפרש"י על פ' ראשית גוים עמלק שהוא נזדווג לישראל תחלה משל לאמבטי רותחת וכו' בא זהו הפשירה בפניהם, נמצא שממנו למד והכל להזדווג לישראל להזיק להם ח"ו. ומסיק בגמרא שלא נכתבו כולם אלא להגדיל תורה ויאדיר כי באמת ע" יהד' אבות נזיקין שהם הד' מלכיות על ידם דייקא יגדיל תורה ויאדיר כי אח"כ מוציאין מהם בלעם מפיהם בבחי' חיל בלע ויקיאנו. ועושין מזה תורה שנקראת אשר חיל נמצא שדייקא על ידם נגדלת התורה:
וזשארז"ל אבות מכלל דאיכא תולדות כי אלו הד' מלכיות הם כלליו הע' אומין נמצא שיש להם תולדות דהיינו הע' אומין שמתפשטין מהם:
segments.en:
And this is “and he did not fear G–d” — namely, the blemish of Malchus and kavod, for the essence of kavod is yirah [awe] — to be in awe before His glory, may He be blessed, in the aspect of “to fear the honored, glorious Name” (Deuteronomy 28:58).

Therefore Amalaik is the aspect of forgetfulness (shich’chah), as is known, for he causes the aspect of “an elder who has forgotten his learning,” through the weariness of the nefesh, through the blemish of tefillah, as mentioned above. Therefore there is a mitzvah to remember the deeds of Amalaik, in order to rectify the aspect of forgetfulness mentioned above.

And this is what is written: “And Amalaik came and fought with Israel in Refidim” (Exodus 17:8). And our Sages of blessed memory said: “[biR’fidim] — in laxity of hands (rifyon yadayim)” — this is the aspect of laxity and weariness of the nefesh. For the growth and strengthening of the nefesh comes through the aspect of the hands, in the aspect of “and in Your hand to make great and to strengthen” (I Chronicles 29:12), as explained there in the discourse “And [Hashem] built” mentioned above. See there. And so, when there is laxity of hands, G–d forbid, it is the aspect of weariness of the nefesh, and then “Amalaik came,” as mentioned above.

And this is what is written first: “And they encamped at Refidim, and there was no water to drink” (Exodus 17:1). For there, in the laxity of hands, which is the aspect of weariness of the nefesh, they needed water — the aspect of “cold waters” mentioned above. But they blemished further: “And the people quarreled with Moshe” — and they blemished the kavod of the elder. Therefore Moshe cried out to Hashem: “What shall I do with this people? A little more and they will stone me!” (Exodus 17:4) — for “I do not know what to do for them, for the matter depends on me — through their giving me kavod,” as mentioned above, and they are blemishing this further, and through this they cause the aspect of forgetfulness to the elder.

And this is “a little more and they will stone me” — this is the aspect of forgetfulness, which is the aspect of death, as Rabbainu, whose light should shine, wrote (Likutay Moharan I, 37). And this is “m’at” [a little] — it is the aspect of forgetfulness, which is mochin d’katnus [constricted consciousness], as is known.

Therefore Hashem, may He be blessed, answered him: “Pass before the people” (Exodus 17:5) — and you will see that they will conduct themselves with kavod toward you, in the manner that Rashi explained there. And then it was indeed rectified. And he took the staff, which is the aspect of a ruling scepter, the aspect of Malchus, as our Sages of blessed memory said: “Take a staff and strike upon their skulls; one spokesman for the generation,” etc. And through this he struck the rock, which is the aspect of a stone upon the mouth of the well — which is the aspect of clouds that cover the eyes, through which it is impossible to draw from the waters of da’as [knowledge], the aspect of “cold waters” mentioned above. And through striking the rock with the staff, as mentioned above — which is the aspect of “thunders” — through this, great waters came forth, the aspect of “cold waters,” “and the congregation and their livestock drank” (Numbers 20:11). And all the nefashos were rectified and revived from their weariness. See well in the discourse “And [Hashem] built” mentioned above, regarding the aspects of “thunders” and “cold waters.” See there.

Therefore the passage of Amalaik is juxtaposed [to this], for through that very blemish which was not yet fully rectified, as it is written “because of their testing,” etc. (Exodus 17:7) — therefore “Amalaik came,” as mentioned above. And therefore the war with Amalaik was dependent on tefillah with kavanah, as it is written: “And it was, when Moshe raised his hand, Israel prevailed” (Exodus 17:11). And our Sages of blessed memory said: “Were the hands of Moshe [winning or losing the war]? Rather, when Israel would gaze upward and direct their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they would prevail,” etc. (Rosh HaShanah 29a). For the essence of the victory over Amalaik was dependent on the intention of the heart in tefillah, to rectify the weariness of the nefesh, as mentioned above. And all of this was dependent on Moshe, for from him is drawn the aspect of “cold waters,” as mentioned above.

§ 4

It emerges that through returning a lost object, the aspect of holy Malchus, the aspect of kavod, is rectified. For just as the nefesh is weary when it falls and becomes lost and distanced from its “mother” — namely, the kavod — so too is the power of Malchus and kavod blemished and weakened when the nefashos are distant from it, for “there is no king without a people”.

Therefore, the kingship of Israel began initially through returning a lost object — that Shaul went to seek his father’s lost [donkeys]. And this is what is written: “And as for the donkeys that were lost… do not set your heart upon them, for they have been found. And to whom does all the desire of Israel belong?” etc. (I Samuel 9:20). For this depends on that, as mentioned above.

And all of this came about because they blemished through their request, saying: “Give us a king to judge us, like all the nations” (I Samuel 8:5). It turns out that they distanced themselves from the kavod, for the kavod belongs exclusively to Israel, in the aspect of “And in their assembly, let my honor not be joined” (Genesis 49:6), as Rabbainu, whose light should shine, wrote. But the wicked kingdom, which is the aspect of Aisav-Amalaik, is in the aspect of “despised are you exceedingly” (Obadiah 1:2). And they said, “Give us a king like all the nations,” and they distanced themselves from the kavod and blemished the kavod of the elder — namely, Shmuel — as it is written at the beginning of the passage: “And it was, when Shmuel grew old” (I Samuel 8:1). For they needed to be careful with his kavod, through which the kingship of Israel would be rectified, as mentioned above. And as is apparent there in the verses — that they blemished this greatly, for they were not careful with the kavod of Shmuel. Therefore, Hashem arranged the matter so that there would be a lost item near the place of the kingship — namely, in the house of Kish, father of Shaul. And afterwards, when the lost item was found, then the kingship was rectified, in the aspect of “And as for the lost donkeys… and to whom does all the desire of Israel belong? Is it not to you and to all your father’s house?” as mentioned above (I Samuel 9, 10, 13).

Therefore he was warned: “Seven days shall you wait until I come to you” (I Samuel 10:8). For his kingship depended on this — to be very careful with the kavod of Shmuel, as mentioned above, in order to rectify the blemish mentioned above. And therefore, when he was not careful with this, his kingship was annulled, as it is written: “And now your kingdom shall not endure” etc. (I Samuel 13:14). For the rectification of the kingship depended on the kavod of Shmuel, as mentioned above.

Therefore, the passage of Amalaik was immediately juxtaposed, and he was commanded to destroy Amalaik. For then he needed to gird his loins to fight Amalaik, since they had not been careful with the aspect of rectifying the return of the nefesh to the kavod, as mentioned above, and then comes the war of Amalaik, as mentioned above. And this is what Rashi explained there: “And now, hear the voice of the word of Hashem” (I Samuel 15:1) — “once you acted foolishly; now hear,” etc. This is connected to this, for the war of Amalaik comes through the blemish mentioned above — that he blemished the kavod of the elder, as mentioned above. And therefore he needed to be careful now to erase the memory of Amalaik, lest he grow strong, G–d forbid. And since he was not careful even with this, his kingship was torn away completely, as mentioned above.

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: that Shaul was punished for not insisting on his kavod, as it is written: “And they despised him, and he was as one who was silent” (I Samuel 10:27). For he certainly needed to insist on his kavod, for the rectification of the kingship is through the kavod, as mentioned above. And therefore Shmuel said to him: “Is it not so that even if you are small in your own eyes, you are the head of the tribes of Israel?” (I Samuel 15:17) — and you needed to be careful with your kavod, for that is the essence of the rectification of the kingship, as mentioned above. And because he did not insist on his kavod, through this he caused the war of Amalaik, as mentioned above, and he needed to be very careful now to subdue him. And because he blemished even in this, his kingship was torn away.

It emerges that all these blemishes were connected to each other, and because he was not careful with them, his kingship was discontinued. Therefore [Shmuel] tore his garment — to indicate that the entire essence of the blemish is the aspect of blemishing the kavod, which is the aspect of a “garment” (levush), as mentioned above. As they said (Bava Kama 91b): Rabbi Yochanan called his garments “my honorers” (m’chab’dusai). And through this they caused that Shmuel said “indeed, before Hashem’s anointed” (I Samuel 16:6), and Hashem, may He be blessed, responded to him: “Do not look at his appearance” (I Samuel 16:7) — which is the aspect of a blemish in the da’as of Shmuel the prophet, the aspect of “an elder who has forgotten his learning,” in proportion to the greatness of his stature.

§ 5

And this is when Shmuel rebuked them for having blemished his kavod and having asked for a king, he said: “Is it not… and he called to Hashem, and He sent thunder and rain” (I Samuel 12:17–18) — namely, he told them that even now he has the power to draw down the aspect of “thunders” and “cold waters” — and this is “thunder and rain.” And this is what Rashi explained: “And you should not have blemished my kavod, since I have this power” — to draw down the aspect of “thunders” and “cold waters,” as mentioned above.

And this is what is stated: “And they drew water and poured it out before Hashem” (I Samuel 7:6). And Rashi and the Targum explain there that they poured out their hearts like water — namely, tefillah with kavanah. And this is the aspect of the verse: “Pour out your heart like water before the face of Hashem” (Lamentations 2:19) — which speaks of tefillah with kavanah; namely, that the prayer should be with intention, in order to revive and restore the nefesh through this. And this is “like water” — the aspect of “cold waters upon a weary soul” mentioned above (Proverbs 25:25).

§ 6

Therefore, the shepherds and kings of Israel were first shepherds and keepers of flocks — like Yaakov and David and Moshe Rabbainu, peace be upon him. For through guarding the flock so that they would not be lost — which is the aspect of guarding the nefesh so that it does not become distanced from the kavod — through this they merited kingship, for this is the aspect of the rectification of Malchus, as mentioned above.

Therefore the prophet rebukes the shepherds in this very language of the blemish of loss — that they are not guarding them — as he said (Ezekiel 34) regarding the shepherds: “Lost sheep were My people… the lost ones you did not seek”. For the essence of the rectification of the aspect of Malchus is through the aspect of returning the lost object — namely, returning the nefesh to the kavod. For the king must guard his people, who are the nefashos, so that they do not scatter and become distanced to the outside and become lost, G–d forbid.

segments.he: וזשארז"ל האי מאן דבעי למיהוי חסידא ליקיים מילי דנזזיקין. חסיד זה בחי' אברהם אשי החסד ששלימות עליית המלכות מן הד' מלכיות על ידו בבחי' והוכן בחסד כסא וע"כ רדף אחרי הד' מלכים כ"ש כ"ז במאמר מישרא הנ"ל. וזה ליקיים מילי דנזיקין להכניע הד' מלכיות ארבעה אבות נזיקין ואזי היא בחי' חסיד בחי' אברהם איש החסד כנ"ל:
segments.en:
And this is what is written regarding David (Psalms 78:71–72): “From behind the nursing ewes He brought him, to shepherd Yaakov His people.” For through guarding the flock exceedingly with a compassionate eye, so that they would not be lost, G–d forbid, through this he merited to be king, to shepherd His people Israel. For this is the rectification of Malchus, as mentioned above, in the aspect of returning the nefashos to the kavod, as mentioned above.

And this is: “And he shepherded them with the integrity of his heart” — this is the aspect of tefillah with kavanah, where his mouth and heart are equal. And this is the aspect of tam laivav [integrity of heart] — that his heart is not divided from his mouth. And through the aspect of “integrity of his heart,” the aspect of tefillah with kavanah, the aspect of the drawing near of the nefesh to the kavod — through this comes the rectification of Malchus, as mentioned above. And this is: “And he shepherded them with the integrity of his heart” — according to the integrity of his heart, so was he a shepherd and king, as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of “and with the skill of his hands he guided them” — these are the aspect of the hands which make the nefashos grow and become strong, as mentioned above.

§ 7

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: “If he was an elder and it is not befitting his dignity (kavod)” — regarding this it says: “and you may hide yourself” (Deuteronomy 22:1). For the lost object is the aspect of the distancing of the nefesh from the kavod, as mentioned above, and then it is in the aspect of a “weary soul,” as mentioned above. And the essential rectification for this depends on the kavod of the elder, as mentioned above. For when there is a lost object, a certain blemish reaches the da’as of the elder, the aspect of “an elder who has forgotten his learning,” as mentioned above — for this depends on that, as mentioned above.

Therefore, the Torah commanded “and you may hide yourself” — so that the elder does not blemish his kavod through the lost object. For on the contrary, now one must be very careful with the kavod of the elder — and this itself is the aspect of the rectification of the lost object, as mentioned above.

§ 8

And this is what is written in the Shulchan Aruch [Code of Jewish Law]: “A lost object of a gentile is permitted [to keep], and it is forbidden to return it,” etc. “And if he returned it for the sake of kiddush Hashem [sanctification of G–d’s Name], it is permitted. And in a place where there would be chillul Hashem [desecration of G–d’s Name], he is obligated to return it,” etc.

For the gentile nations have no portion in the kavod; for the kavod belongs only to Israel, but they are in the aspect of “despised are you exceedingly,” as mentioned above. Therefore, their lost object is certainly permitted, for the essence of returning a lost object is to return the nefesh to the kavod, as mentioned above. And on the contrary, it is forbidden to return it, for the nefashos that are in the hands of the nations are like birds caught in a trap, and since they have escaped from the fowler’s snare, it is a great mitzvah that a Jew should acquire them — for there is the kavod — in order to revive them, to return them to the kavod.

Therefore, in a place where there is kiddush Hashem, where the Name of Heaven will be sanctified and honored through returning the lost object to the gentile, then it is permitted to return it. For through this one causes kavod shamayim [honor of Heaven]. Therefore, even though he returns it to the gentile, it is nevertheless in the aspect of returning the nefesh to the kavod, since G–d’s honor, may He be blessed, is sanctified and magnified through this, as mentioned above. And similarly, in a place where there would be chillul Hashem, he is obligated to return it, so as not to blemish kavod shamayim, G–d forbid, through the lost object. For the essence of the rectification of the lost object is through the aspect of rectifying the kavod, as mentioned above.

§ 10

And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: “If his father told him, ‘Do not return the lost object,’ he should not listen to him” (Bava Metzia 32a). For returning the lost object is the aspect of rectifying the kavod, as mentioned above. And therefore, one might have thought (havah amina) that honoring one’s father should override this mitzvah, for honoring one’s father is also the aspect of rectifying the kavod — for the root of one’s soul is in one’s father and mother, where one’s soul is clothed, and the primary clothing of the soul is in the kavod, as mentioned above. Therefore he is obligated to honor them, for they are his kavod, for there his soul is clothed.

And therefore the Torah teaches us that even so, their honor does not override the mitzvah of returning a lost object, which is also the aspect of rectifying the kavod, as mentioned above. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said: “His father told him, ‘Do not return’ — one might think he should listen to him? The verse teaches: ‘I am Hashem’ — all of you are obligated in My honor.” “In My honor” precisely, for this is the aspect of rectifying the kavod, as mentioned above.

§ 11

And this is why our Sages of blessed memory established and placed the laws of the kavod of one’s teacher and the kavod of one’s father specifically in connection with a lost object, as they said in the Mishnah (Bava Metzia 33a): “His father’s lost object and his teacher’s lost object,” etc. For a son or student must pursue the lost object of his father and teacher all the more, since he is obligated in their kavod, and returning a lost object is also the rectification of the kavod, as mentioned above.

Therefore Shaul went to seek his father’s lost [donkeys], for the son must pursue his father’s lost object, and then the kavod is completed and greatly rectified, as mentioned above. And likewise the student for his teacher, as mentioned above. And therefore they established the laws of their kavod specifically in connection with a lost object, as mentioned above.

§ 12

Therefore, the found object (metziah) of one’s son and daughter belongs to the father. And as long as they eat at his table, they are considered minors (k’tanim), and their found objects belong to their father. For when the finder acquires the found object for himself, he returns the nefesh to the portion of kavod that is his own and he acquires it. Therefore, minors — as long as they eat at their father’s table, their found objects belong to him. For the table is the aspect of kavod, the aspect of “a king’s table,” as is explained there. And therefore, as long as they eat from his table, they are attached to his kavod, and they must return their found objects to him, for there is their kavod, since they eat from his.

§ 13

Also, all acquisitions (z’chiyos) are through da’as [knowledge/mind]. Therefore a minor has no capacity for acquisition, for he has no da’as. And likewise a deaf-mute and one who lacks mental competence (shoteh). For wealth is the root of the nefesh, and its root is in da’as, for da’as is the root of all sustenance, in the aspect of “and through knowledge the chambers are filled” (Proverbs 24:4). For wealth and the nefashos are the aspect of g’vuros [strengths/severities], as Rabbainu, whose light should shine, wrote — that their root is in da’as. And similarly it is implied in his words many times that wealth depends on da’as. And this is the aspect of “In the shadow of wisdom, in the shadow of money” (Ecclesiastes 7:12).

Therefore, whoever has no da’as has no capacity for acquisition in any form of wealth — that is, in any object. And this is the aspect of ya’ush [despair/renunciation] that effects acquisition in a found object. For ya’ush is when one diverts his mind (da’as) from the matter, as they said: “Despair that is not conscious (ya’ush shelo mida’as) is not [valid] despair” (Bava Metzia 21b). For he must know that he lost [the object] and consciously despair of it. It turns out that he removes his da’as from that object which he lost, and therefore he no longer has any acquisition in it, as mentioned above.

Therefore, they are considered minors regarding found objects as long as they eat at their father’s table, and their found objects belong to their father. For the essence of da’as comes through eating, as Rabbainu wrote in the discourse “And it was, as they were emptying their sacks” (Likutay Moharan I, 17). Therefore, as long as they eat at his table, their da’as is attached to their father. Therefore their found objects belong to him, and he acquires the found objects of his children, for the essence of acquisition is through da’as, as mentioned above.

segments.he: וזה שאמר ועוד (שם) לקיים מילי דאבות היינו הך. כי שלימות המלכות על ידי האבות כנ"ל:
